Estimate the additive genetic covariance matrix

Source: R/fit_G.R
fit_G.Rd

Fits a multivariate animal model on many small trait subsets and reassembles the subset estimates into one positive semi-definite matrix. The estimator is LiMMBo's: the speed comes from giving each subset its own nuisance residual covariance, so the many small fits replace one large one.

Usage

fit_G(
  Y,
  X = NULL,
  A,
  s = NULL,
  min_cooccurrence = NULL,
  subsets = NULL,
  engine = "stanimal",
  engine_args = list(),
  assembly = c("ls", "average"),
  weights = c("none", "inverse_variance"),
  missing = c("model", "complete_block"),
  spread = c("mixture", "average"),
  cores = NULL,
  n_draws = 1000L,
  seed = NULL,
  progress = getOption("indri.progress", interactive())
)

Arguments

Y

Phenotype matrix, individuals in rows and traits in columns. Gaps (NA) are allowed with every engine; see missing.

X

Fixed-effect design, one row per individual. Defaults to an intercept. It must have full column rank and be able to represent a constant (an intercept, or the indicators of every level of a factor). stanimal::animal_design() builds Y, X and A from a formula, a data frame and a pedigree: d <- animal_design(cbind(t1, t2) ~ sex + age, dat, pedigree = ped); fit_G(d$Y, d$X, d$A).

A

Relationship matrix, individuals in the same order as Y. When both have row names they are matched by name.

s

Subset size parameter. Controls how many trait pairs each subset covers, not the number of traits in a subset; see indri_subsets(). Defaults to min(floor(sqrt(K)), 3), at least 2 and kept narrow enough that a block never covers every trait: blocks of up to four traits. Larger blocks shrank the stanimal correlations more (and undercovered) and gave the REML engines nothing for their extra cost.

min_cooccurrence

Minimum number of distinct subsets every trait pair must appear in. The default depends on the engine: 3 for "stanimal", 1 for the REML engines, where three distinct contexts per pair measured no better than one (same accuracy and interval coverage at half the cost). Identical subsets are never repeated, since a pair estimated twice in the same trait context adds nothing, so the value is capped at what the block width allows (1 for two-trait blocks).

subsets

Optional precomputed subset matrix, from indri_subsets().

engine

Block engine: "stanimal" (Bayesian, posterior draws, models gaps in Y), "sommer", "asreml" or "wombat" (REML, with uncertainty from each block's sampling covariance; much faster for large N). "wombat" runs the external WOMBAT program; see indri_engine().

engine_args

List of arguments passed to the engine's fit function.

assembly

"ls" fits the closest positive semi-definite matrix to all the subset estimates; "average" keeps the plain average, nudged onto the positive semi-definite cone.

weights

"none" for LiMMBo's equal weights, or "inverse_variance" to weight each subset estimate by its reported uncertainty (per-entry standard error for REML engines, per-entry posterior variance for the draws-based stanimal engine). Weights apply to both the average and the projection.

missing

What to do with gaps in Y. "model" (the default) keeps every observed value and lets the engine handle the gaps: stanimal integrates them out, and the REML engines use each individual's observed traits (a missing value is one missing record, not a missing individual). "complete_block" drops incomplete individuals once, before subsetting; it discards information (with 15% of values missing at random, a third of the individuals and about 20% wider standard errors).

spread

How G_draws and corrG_draws combine the block posteriors. "mixture" (the default) takes each entry of each draw from one covering block at random; "average" averages draw d across the covering blocks. Blocks are fitted to the same individuals, so averaging their independent chains is overconfident by roughly the square root of a pair's coverage (40% coverage of the true correlations at nominal 95%, against 95-97% for the mixture at the default settings). See indri_assemble_draws().

cores

Total number of concurrent processes for the whole fit, not the number of subsets to run at once. Defaults to 1, except for "asreml", which defaults to 2: every worker checks out its own ASReml licence seat, and a standard licence allows two at once, on one machine at a time. When asreml is already loaded in the session (which usually holds a seat) the default drops to 1 and the blocks are fitted in-session. Use cores = 1 with a single-seat licence; more workers than free seats stop with a licence error. The budget is divided between blocks and chains: a block fit supplies chains processes by default (four for "stanimal", its own default), so cores = 4 with the default engine arguments runs one block at a time with four chains in parallel, while cores = 4 with engine_args = list(chains = 1) runs four blocks at once. chains is never changed here; only how many run concurrently.

n_draws

Number of draws per block for the REML engines, which report a joint sampling covariance of each block's G entries (the inverse average-information matrix) instead of posterior draws: indri draws from that normal approximation and assembles the draws like stanimal's. Ignored for "stanimal".

seed

Optional seed for the subset construction. The engine's sampler seed is passed through engine_args.

progress

Show a progress bar of the block fits (blocks done, elapsed time, an estimate of the time left) on the console. Defaults to getOption("indri.progress", interactive()): on in an interactive session, off under Rscript. With parallel blocks the bar updates after each load-balanced round of about four blocks per worker. Engine output (for example CmdStan's own progress) is printed as before; silence it with engine_args = list(refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE) for stanimal.

Value

An object of class indri_fit. The estimate is G, in the units of Y, with corrG its correlation matrix; G_bar (the average before projection) and sigma_G are in the units of Y too. E is the residual covariance, for indri_gwas(): the covariance of the residuals of Y on X minus the assembled G (scaled for the relatedness in A), with eigenvalues floored at 1e-3 of the largest. E_bar is the average of the block residual covariances, for reference: at many traits it is not a covariance matrix, and a projection of it miscalibrates the association tests. blocks holds the raw standardised-scale block fits. G_draws and corrG_draws (traits x traits x draws) carry the assembled block uncertainty, from the posterior draws of "stanimal" blocks or from the normal sampling approximation of the REML blocks (see n_draws); use corrG_draws for intervals on correlations, since it mixes each block's own correlation draws and stays within [-1, 1]. Mixed draws are pointwise: their entries are drawn independently, so a single draw need not be positive semi-definite, and they support per-entry intervals, not functions of the whole matrix. Neither is a posterior over the joint matrix.

Details

Traits are standardised once, using every observed value, before the subsets are drawn. Every engine therefore sees the same numbers and estimates the same matrix on the same scale, whatever it does internally; the fixed effects in X are handled inside each block fit. Assembly and the positive semi-definite projection also run on that scale, and the assembled covariances (G, G_bar, G_draws, sigma_G) are then returned in the units of Y. The raw block fits in blocks stay on the standardised scale: do not combine them directly with the assembled outputs (y_sd converts between the two).

References

Meyer, H. V., Casale, F. P., Stegle, O., and Birney, E. (2018). LiMMBo: a simple, scalable approach for linear mixed models in high-dimensional genetic association studies. bioRxiv, preprint. doi:10.1101/255497

Examples

# \donttest{
# This example fits six small Stan models and needs stanimal and CmdStan.
if (requireNamespace("stanimal", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !is.na(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(error_on_NA = FALSE))) {
  K <- 4L
  N <- 60L
  # Twelve families of five full siblings.
  A <- kronecker(diag(12), matrix(0.5, 5, 5))
  diag(A) <- 1
  G_true <- matrix(0.2, K, K)
  diag(G_true) <- 0.8
  E_true <- diag(0.6, K)
  X <- cbind(intercept = 1, group = rep(c(0, 1), length.out = N))
  genetic <- t(chol(A)) %*% matrix(rnorm(N * K), N, K) %*% chol(G_true)
  residual <- matrix(rnorm(N * K), N, K) %*% chol(E_true)
  Y <- genetic + residual + X[, "group"] %o% c(0.2, -0.2, 0.1, 0)
  colnames(Y) <- paste0("trait", seq_len(K))

  # These short chains are for a quick example, not reliable inference.
  # For real work, use more chains and iterations and check diagnostics.
  fit <- fit_G(Y, X = X, A = A, subsets = t(utils::combn(K, 2)),
               engine = "stanimal", cores = 1,
               engine_args = list(chains = 2, iter = 400,
                                  refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE))
  fit$corrG
  fit$coverage
  fit$diagnostics

  # G is in the units of Y; the standardised-scale estimate, if needed:
  G_std <- diag(1 / fit$y_sd) %*% fit$G %*% diag(1 / fit$y_sd)
  fit$sigma_G

  # Pointwise correlation spread, not a joint posterior interval.
  quantile(fit$corrG_draws[1, 2, ], c(0.025, 0.975))
}
